The left tomato has a more advanced lesion with dark grayish-black spore masses in concentric rings; the right shows an earlier stage with a pinkish-tan margin and dark center. This pattern strongly suggests Anthracnose or possibly Alternaria/Gray Mold on fruit.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Two ripe orange-red tomatoes with large circular, sunken lesions. The left has advanced dark grayish-black spore masses in concentric rings; the right shows an earlier stage with a pinkish-tan margin around a dark spore center. This is classic fruit rot morphology.

- **Anthracnose/Bugwood_17**: Ripe red tomato with a large circular, sunken lesion showing concentric rings and a dark spore mass center — nearly identical pattern to the test image. This is the best match.

- **Alternaria/Bugwood_4**: Stem canker, not fruit — no match.
- **Gray_Mold/Bugwood_13**: Cracked green tomato with diffuse rot — no match.
- **Rhizopus_Soft_Rots/Bugwood_1**: Microscopic view only.
- **Early_Blight/CDDM_1107**: Mostly leaf lesions; illustrated fruit lesion less definitive.
- **Late_Blight/CDDM_498**: Leaf browning, no fruit lesions.

The circular sunken lesions with concentric rings and dark acervuli (spore masses) on ripe tomato fruit is the hallmark of Anthracnose.
